written: 2026-09-27, committed before any return of this rule on these ETFs was computed
hypothesis: Faber's 10-month moving-average timing rule, applied to five asset-class ETFs held in equal weights, earns positive alpha over simply holding the same five ETFs equal-weighted.
source: Mebane T. Faber, 'A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation', working paper May 2006, The Journal of Wealth Management Spring 2007 (SSRN 962461). Rule text: 'Buy when monthly price > 10-month SMA. Sell and move to cash when monthly price < 10-month SMA.' Updated once a month on the last day of the month; total return series; cash = 90-day T-bills.
why_out_of_sample: The rule was published in May 2006. Every ETF-era day tested here comes after that. The rule is not tuned: one config is registered.
rule: At each month-end close, for each ETF: hold its 20% if its total-return price (adj_close) is above the mean of its last 10 month-end prices, else hold that 20% in T-bills. Weights reset to 20% each month. Signal and trade at the same month-end close, as in the paper.
costs: 10 bps per side on each month's change in weights
cash: ^IRX 13-week T-bill yield / 252 per day, lagged one day
benchmark: PRIMARY: the same five ETFs held 20% each, rebalanced monthly (the paper's own comparison), total returns. SECONDARY, non-gating: regression on SPY and IEF; 60/40 SPY/IEF; SPY.

pass_rule.statistic: Newey-West (21 lags) t of the daily alpha of (strategy - T-bills) regressed on (primary benchmark - T-bills)

power_note: About 19.4 years: at t >= 2 the test can detect an information ratio of about 0.45 or more. A smaller real edge would read as 'not significant'.

consequences.pass: Propose it as a replacement Meridian sleeve (for the SPY/XLK trend sleeve and/or the no-edge sleeves); a fund-level backtest on the honest baseline follows, and it needs the user's OK before anything changes live.
consequences.positive_not_significant: No live change. Run it as a shadow sleeve (signals logged, no orders) from 2026-10-01 and judge it on 2027-09-30.

paper_caveat: Alpaca paper pays no dividends or interest, so a live paper version would understate the T-bill share and the ETF dividends.
